title_en: Wuxi Zhanggui Wireless Network Technology Co., Ltd. v. Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over network service contract
ruling_gist_en: Both parties, fully aware that the electronic messages they sent were commercial advertisements, nevertheless disregarded the subjective willingness of mobile phone users to receive such commercial advertising information, and forcibly sent commercial advertising text messages to unspecified members of the public, thereby infringing upon the interests of the general public. The text messages so sent shall be deemed spam messages, the relevant contracts executed by the parties shall be void, and the consideration involved shall constitute illegal gains which the people's court shall confiscate.

full_text_en:
Wuxi Zhanggui Wireless Network Technology Co., Ltd. v. Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd.
— dispute over network service contract

Ruling Summary

Where both parties clearly know that the electronic information to be sent is commercial advertising in nature, yet they disregard the subjective willingness of mobile phone user groups to consent to receiving commercial advertising information, forcibly send commercial advertising short messages to unspecified members of the public, and thereby infringe upon the interests of the public, the short messages so sent shall be determined as spam messages, the relevant contracts concluded are void, and the consideration involved constitutes illegal gains, which shall be confiscated by the people's court.

Plaintiff: Wuxi Zhanggui Wireless Network Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Changjiang North Road, Wuxi New District, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Zhong Congjiang, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hongxing Road, Nanchang District, Wuxi, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Hua Lingyan, Chairperson of the company.
Administrator: Liquidation Group of Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd.

Wuxi Zhanggui Wireless Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhanggui Network Company) filed a lawsuit with the Nanchang District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province against the defendant Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiabao Company) over a dispute concerning a network service contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations

On April 23, 2013, Zhanggui Network Company entered into an "Enterprise Short Message Publication Business Cooperation Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Short Message Cooperation Agreement") with the defendant Jiabao Company, stipulating that Zhanggui Network Company would provide targeted mobile information publication services to Jiabao Company at unit prices of: RMB 0.04 per message for ordinary short messages, and RMB 0.1 per message for community targeted investment. Jiabao Company would pay Zhanggui Network Company according to the total contract amount specified in the "Information Service Execution Confirmation Form" confirmed by both parties, and Jiabao Company was required to pay Zhanggui Network Company for the executed information costs in the following month. By the time of litigation, Zhanggui Network Company had executed information services totaling RMB 84,000, but Jiabao Company failed to pay such costs as agreed. After repeated demands for payment yielded no results, Zhanggui Network Company filed the lawsuit with the court, requesting the court to order: 1. Jiabao Company to immediately pay the information service fees overdue to Zhanggui Network Company in the total amount of RMB 84,000; and 2. Jiabao Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

In support of its claims, the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company submitted the following evidence:

1. One copy of the "Short Message Cooperation Agreement," to prove the rights and obligations between the parties.
2. Ten copies of "Information Service Execution Confirmation Forms," to prove that Zhanggui Network Company had performed its contractual obligations as agreed and that the performance had been confirmed by Jiabao Company.
3. Three copies of the stub of tax invoices and one receipt, to prove that Zhanggui Network Company, at the request of Jiabao Company, issued the invoices in advance, but Jiabao Company did not actually pay the corresponding amounts.

Upon cross-examination, the defendant Jiabao Company had no objections to the above evidence.

Defense by the Administrator of the Defendant Jiabao Company

The administrator of the defendant Jiabao Company argued: It had no objections to the facts alleged by the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company or to the amount of the information service fees, and requested that the court handle the matter in accordance with the law.

The defendant Jiabao Company did not submit any evidence.

Based on the evidence presented and the cross-examination conducted, the evidence submitted by the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company all satisfied the formal requirements for evidence and could be used as evidence.

Facts Found by the Court

On April 23, 2013, the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company and the defendant Jiabao Company entered into a "Short Message Cooperation Agreement," stipulating that Zhanggui Network Company would publish for Jiabao Company the relevant mobile information services it provided at the times, with the content, within the regions, and targeting the mobile phone user groups designated by Jiabao Company; the unit prices were RMB 0.04 per message for ordinary short messages and RMB 0.1 per message for community targeted investment; due to the uncertainty of adjustments at any time regarding the time, content, region, and mobile phone user groups during the execution of the mobile information services, the sending time, content, region, and mobile phone user groups would not serve as annexes to the contract; Jiabao Company should pay the full mobile information sending service fees to Zhanggui Network Company in accordance with the time and corresponding payment methods determined by the "Information Service Execution Confirmation Form"; based on confidentiality obligations, Zhanggui Network Company was entitled not to disclose to Jiabao Company the mobile phone user data in its possession; Jiabao Company should make payment according to the total contract amount specified in the "Information Service Execution Confirmation Form" confirmed by both parties, and Jiabao Company should pay Zhanggui Network Company for the information costs already executed in the following month; when making payment, Jiabao Company should strictly verify the corresponding invoices provided by Zhanggui Network Company and the "Collection Authority Letter" affixed with the official seal of Zhanggui Network Company; otherwise, any financial loss caused thereby should be borne by Jiabao Company.

On May 10 and May 25 of the same year, Huang Wei, the sales supervisor of the defendant Jiabao Company, signed two "Information Service Execution Confirmation Forms" issued by the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company to Jiabao Company. The confirmation forms mainly stated: "... The information services commissioned from Zhanggui Network Company in May 2013 have been fully executed. The specific execution details are as follows: Information service time: May 10, 2013; Quantity of information services: 100,000 messages; Unit price: RMB 0.04; Total amount: RMB 4,000; Information service content: Quality luxury homes, grand finale! Core mature supporting facilities at Taihu Square, 360-degree canal view, 93-388 sqm full-scale ultimate prosperity! Central Mansion grand opening in May! 83333888 [Jingui Daguan]"; and "... The information services commissioned from Zhanggui Network Company in May 2013 have been fully executed. The specific execution details are as follows: Information service time: May 25, 2013; Quantity of information services: 100,000 messages; Unit price: RMB 0.04; Total amount: RMB 4,000; Information service content: Fine products for all! [Jingui Daguan] Central Imperial View Mansion is about to be released. Full stone dry-hanging, smart home. Proudly situated in the CBD of Taihu Square, enjoying an upper-class life. 83333888 [Jingui Daguan]."

On June 12, June 17, June 21, June 25, June 26, June 29, June 30, and July 27, 2013, Zhu Yuefeng, the sales director of the defendant Jiabao Company, signed eight "Information Service Execution Confirmation Forms," confirming that the outstanding service fees owed to the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company were RMB 10,000, RMB 10,000, RMB 8,000, RMB 8,000, RMB 10,000, RMB 10,000, RMB 10,000, and RMB 10,000 respectively. These eight confirmation forms all specified the information service time, quantity, unit price, subtotal amount, total amount, and other details, and the information service content was real estate sales advertisements similar to those in the aforementioned two "Information Service Execution Confirmation Forms."

The cumulative amount under the above ten "Information Service Execution Confirmation Forms" was RMB 84,000.

On May 31, July 1, and September 3, 2013, the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company issued three invoices to the defendant Jiabao Company, in the amounts of RMB 8,000, RMB 66,000, and RMB 10,000, totaling RMB 84,000. At the same time, on the invoice receipt of Zhanggui Network Company, Jiang Zhongfen, the financial staff member of Jiabao Company, signed as the recipient, confirming receipt of the above three invoices.

During the trial, the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company stated: 1. The concept of "community targeted investment" as stipulated in the "Short Message Cooperation Agreement" referred to Zhanggui Network Company's targeted distribution of short messages based on the customer mobile phone numbers provided by the defendant Jiabao Company; the concept of "ordinary short messages" referred to Zhanggui Network Company's random distribution after searching for mobile phone numbers with Wuxi area codes online; Zhanggui Network Company was not aware of the specific recipients of the messages; 2. Zhanggui Network Company did not verify whether the mobile phone users provided by Jiabao Company consented to receiving the information; 3. The cost of sending the short messages could not be calculated and no basis for the cost could be provided.

The administrator of the defendant Jiabao Company stated: Among the mobile phone users provided by Jiabao Company to Zhanggui Network Company for sending short messages, no consent was obtained from the mobile phone users.

It was further found that the business scope of the defendant Jiabao Company included real estate development and operation. On October 15, 2014, the court ruled to accept the reorganization application filed by Bank of Jiangsu Co., Ltd., Wuxi Branch, and others against Jiabao Company, and designated the Liquidation Group of Wuxi Jiabao Real Estate Co., Ltd. as the administrator of Jiabao Company.

Opinion of the Court

In entering into and performing contracts, the parties shall comply with laws and administrative regulations, respect social morality, and must not disrupt the social economic order or harm the public interest. In this case, according to the "Short Message Cooperation Agreement" entered into by the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company and the defendant Jiabao Company, and the statements of both parties, both parties clearly knew the nature of the electronic information to be sent, yet they disregarded the subjective willingness of mobile phone user groups to consent to receiving commercial advertising information, forcibly sent commercial advertising to unspecified members of the public, violating the provisions on the protection of network information and infringing upon the interests of the public. Such a contract should be held void, and the short messages sent should be determined as spam messages. Since Zhanggui Network Company has fully performed its obligations under the agreement and Jiabao Company has actually benefited objectively; and Zhanggui Network Company, as a network service provider, violated the provisions on electronic information publication during the formation and performance of the contract, intentionally sent spam messages to unspecified members of the public, acted in an egregious manner, and should be sanctioned; therefore, this court separately issues a decision to confiscate the service fees.

In conclusion, the Nanchang District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 7 and Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 7 and Article 11 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Strengthening the Protection of Network Information, rendered a judgment on December 11, 2014:

The claims of the plaintiff Zhanggui Network Company are dismissed.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and the judgment has become legally effective.

On December 31, 2014, the Nanchang District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 134, paragraph 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 163 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation), and Article 7 and Article 11 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Strengthening the Protection of Network Information, issued a civil sanction decision:

The service fees of RMB 84,000 owed by Jiabao Company to Zhanggui Network Company are confiscated.

After the decision was served, Jiabao Company did not apply for reconsideration within the statutory period, and the decision has become legally effective.
